prompt: A circular garden path has radius $10$ ft. A gardener walks along the arc of a $90^\circ$ section. Write the exact arc length in terms of $\pi$ (for example, write $7\pi$ as 7pi).
hint: Arc length is a fraction of the whole circumference: $\frac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi r$.

hints.text: Arc length is a fraction of the whole circumference: $\frac{\theta}{360} \times 2\pi r$.
The whole circumference is $2\pi(10) = 20\pi$, and $90^\circ$ is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the circle.

explanation: Circumference of the whole circle: $C = 2\pi r = 20\pi$ ft.
A $90^\circ$ arc is $\frac{90}{360} = \frac{1}{4}$ of the way around.

alternativeExplanations.title: Fraction first, then multiply
steps: A quarter of $20\pi$ is $5\pi$ — much cleaner than multiplying $20\pi$ by $90$ and dividing by $360$.
